lesson_title: One Stove, One Eggshell, One Bathtub: Grade 10 Physical Geography in a Sitting
hook_text: Why are mountaintops freezing if they're closer to the sun? Your whole Term 1 exam hides in that question.
clip_script: Quick — why is the top of the Drakensberg freezing when it is closer to the sun? Because the sun does not heat the air. It heats the GROUND, and the ground heats the air from below — so climbing a mountain is walking away from the heater. That one sentence unlocks half of Grade 10 geography. It explains convection: air over baked Highveld ground rises like the wobble above a braai fire, cools, and by four o'clock a purple thunderstorm is hailing on Johannesburg. It explains the rain shadow: sea air climbs the mountain, rains itself dry on the way up, and rolls down the far side with nothing left — that is why the Little Karoo is semi-desert one range away from green slopes. And under all of it, the ground itself is moving: the crust is a cracked eggshell, its pieces dragged by slowly churning rock below — squeeze the shell and you fold up the Cape Fold Mountains, snap it and a rift valley drops, slip it suddenly and that jolt is an earthquake. Then the exam gives you a map and asks you to read the land from rings on paper — every contour line a bathtub ring, tight rings for cliffs, a V pointing upstream wherever a river cuts through. One stove, one eggshell, one bathtub: the whole year's physical geography in three pictures you already own.
visual_style: Fast cuts: heat shimmer over red Highveld earth rising into a time-lapse thunderhead; a cross-section mountain with rain on one face and dust on the other; a cracked hard-boiled egg rotating into a globe; contour rings glowing on a draining bathtub that morphs into a 1:50 000 map extract.
mood: Rapid-fire revision energy, confident and playful.
pacing: One-question cold open, three accelerating concept beats, a beat of quiet on the eggshell snap, brisk close on the three-picture recap.
call_to_action: Watch the full revision session and walk into the paper with the whole year folded into three pictures.
